To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the bilinear growth profile is more adequate than the linear or exponential ones for the description of single cell growth in fissions yeast, and that the extended LinBiExp model provides a convenient and accurate fitting tool for such data.
the bilinear and exponential models are equally adequate for fitting single fission yeast cell data, and that the bilinear one is somewhat more adequate for the wee1 Δ mutant.
the bilinear growth model fits the data slightly better than the exponential one and, hence, that the growth profile of individual fission yeast cells is better described by a bilinear model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a quantitative framework for the selection of the most adequate growth model for individual cells, based on the use of model selection criteria.
the development and application of quantitative methods for the analysis of cell growth data and the evaluation of the adequacy of the bilinear and exponential models in the fitting of these data.
the development of a quantitative framework for the selection of adequate growth models and the application of these criteria to the analysis of individual cell growth data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bilinear models should be preferred over the exponential ones in the description of cell growth profiles, but that the issue remains unresolved for now.
the data are consistent with the bilinear model and inconsistent with the exponential model, but the bilinear model cannot be rejected with a high level of confidence.

the bilinear and exponential models are equally adequate for describing the time-profiles of cell size increase in fission yeast, and that the choice between the two is essentially a matter of convenience.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bilinear and exponential models are equally valid, and that both should be considered when modeling cell growth.
the biliner growth profile seems to be the best model for fission yeast cells.

the biliner model is more adequate than the linear model, and the exponential model is more adequate then the linear model, but the bilinear model is only marginally more adequate than the exponeential model, at least for these fission yeast cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of quantitative criteria for model selection should be encouraged in the field of cell cycle research.
, in general, bilinear growth models are to be preferred over exponential ones.
the use of quantitative metrics to compare different models is essential to assess the quality of fits and, hence, to make informed decisions regarding the choice of a given model.
